title: Basis of the Final Bill for a Delivered Event
content:
The final bill on a Private Event & Banquet Services booking is raised the number of calendar days after the event printed against the package, and it gathers food and beverage actually consumed, the billable guest count, room rental, the service charge, audio-visual, any dance floor, additional service hours, security hours and corkage onto one document.

## The service charge

The service charge printed against the package is applied to food and beverage and to additional service hours, and never to room rental, audio-visual or corkage.

| Line on the bill | Carries the service charge |
| --- | --- |
| Food and beverage | Yes |
| Additional service hours | Yes |
| Room rental | No |
| Audio-visual | No |
| Corkage | No |

## Deposits on the bill

The following clause is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis: "Deposits held against the booking are applied to the final bill before it is issued, oldest deposit first, and the bill shows the gross charge, the deposits applied and the balance due."

## The states in which a bill is raised

A final bill is only raised while the agreement stands active or on hold, and where an agreement closes with an event already delivered, the bill is raised against the closing agreement before it is settled out. The state and the unsettled balance are read from the company's records against the agreement's own reference before the bill is raised.

## Goodwill and disputes

A goodwill adjustment may be made on the final bill up to the ceiling printed against the package, as a percentage of the contracted event value, and an adjustment beyond that ceiling is not made at the desk. Where the client disputes a line on the final bill, the undisputed balance falls due on the ordinary terms and only the disputed line is held over.

## Where deposits exceed the charge

Where the deposits applied exceed the gross charge, no bill is raised and the surplus is returned as a deposit refund instead.
